published_source: Figure 4, panel (c) of the published article (Management Science 71(11), 2025, pp. 9628-9649; papers/mnsc/mnsc.2020.01838.pdf): point estimates are plotted, not printed. authors_code_* = output of Replicate.R line 243 on the shipped data, which the figure plots. Panel labels checked against the article (Nov 2).
replication_status: exact (fixest with event_structure reproduces the authors' Replicate.R event coefficients on the authors' sample; see event_structure.verified)
notes: Kang (2025), 'Price-Fixing Cartels and Firm Innovation', Management Science 71(11). Package: Replicate.R + final cleaned/merged .rds files (real processed data; raw DOJ/VitalLaw, PatentsView and licensed Compustat not shipped). FE: unit + 4-digit-NAICS (patents) or Compustat industry group (R&D) x year (authors: felm(... | assignee_id + paste0(cl, year) | 0 | cl)); here xt_vars = naics4 (= cl) so the time FE is year + year x cl; SE clustered by cl. No controls, no weights. Outcomes are IHS-transformed counts/amounts, precomputed as ihs_* (log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)), as in Replicate.R). Formation design (primary set): data_reg_patent_from.rds; treated = colluding assignees observed at formation-relative years -4..-1 and +1..+4 (the formation year itself is not in the file; TimeFromYY = year - formation year, verified), post rows all before breakup; controls = all other patenting assignees 1976-2020 (never treated). gvar g_form = formation year (ID_From); D = 1[year >= g_form] equals the authors' TreatY x POST row by row. 3 treated units with pre-sample formation (1975 or earlier) are always-treated in-sample (kept, as in the authors' sample). Unit id uid = assignee_id except for the one assignee in three cartel episodes (226bee8a..., formations 1988/1995/1998 with overlapping windows, the source of all duplicated assignee-years), which is split into three assignee x episode units so that every unit has one adoption date and no duplicated unit-years; this is the only difference from the authors' regression sample and FE. Event study: authors' TreatY x factor(TimeFromYY), reference -1, coefficients at -4,-3,-2,+1..+4. run_spec rel = year - g_form, so rel = TimeFromYY; rel 0 (formation year) has no rows; pre summary = rel -4..-2, post summary = rel +1..+4 (event_structure; single-year bins, reference -1). Nov 2 audit: event_structure records the authors' bins and reference; sample_filter 'pre_sample_adopter == FALSE' removed, pre-sample adopters kept at their true dates (gvar already holds the calendar year; no adoption_var needed). See the log's Nov 2 section.

event_structure.source: Replicate.R line 243: felm(depvar ~ TreatY + TreatY:TimeFromYY | assignee_id + paste0(cl, year) | 0 | cl) on data_reg_patent_from.rds; TimeFromYY is a factor whose first level is -1, so felm drops TreatY:TimeFromYY-1 (collinear with the unit FE): reference -1 (article, Figure 4 notes: 'Year -1 is used as the baseline'; year 0 omitted). Treated rows exist only at TimeFromYY -4..-1, +1..+4 (window trimmed in the shipped file). gvar g_form = formation year ID_From, so rel = t - g = TimeFromYY in the annual period index (years 1976-2020 consecutive). 'drop': the shipped file contains treated rows only inside the authors' coded window (the event year itself is omitted), so no ever-treated row falls outside bins and ref (0 rows, checked Nov 2); 'drop' and 'ref' are equivalent here. Pre-sample adopters (3 units with event year before 1976) are kept at their true date (gvar holds the calendar year; PROTOCOL Nov 2 ruling (b)); all their in-sample rows are post rows inside the window.
event_structure.verified: fixest (es_assign bins; FE assignee_id + cl^year; cluster cl) on the authors' sample (all 432,448 rows of data_reg_patent_from.rds, incl. the 3 pre-sample units at their true dates) reproduces the 7 coefficients of Replicate.R: max abs diff 2.3e-11 (SE max diff 2.5e-05, felm vs fixest small-sample factor). Pipeline unit id (episode split of one multi-cartel assignee) moves the coefficients by at most 2.3e-04; otherwise the pipeline sample equals the authors'. No numbers are printed in the article; the figure plots the code output on the shipped data.

pipeline_sample_twfe_source: Nov 2: fixest on the pipeline sample (pre-sample adopters kept at true dates, uid FE + cl^year) with event_structure; post (pre) = equal-weight mean of the post_summary (pre_summary) bins, std = post / population SD of y over all estimation rows.
